prior_findings_rule: PRIOR FINDINGS are what earlier runs (deep and quick, including the orchestrator's own conclusions) already established. Start from them and research only the delta since `prior_findings_since`. Do not re-search a finding unless it is expired, it directly drives a number you are about to put in a verdict or proposal, or you have new evidence against it. List ids you re-checked and still hold in `findings_reaffirmed`; put corrections in `findings_revised` as {id, claim, source, reason}. Never restate a prior finding as new.
desk_protocol:
You are one analyst on a desk. You talk to the other analysts through the `comms`
block of your JSON tail; the orchestrator routes every message and nothing in prose is read.

1. ANSWER every message in `desk_inbox`. Each answer:
   {"id": "<message id>", "position": "held" | "revised" | "cannot_answer" | "noted",
    "answer": "<engage the specific point raised>", "evidence": [{"claim","source","date"}],
    "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
    "revision": {<ONLY when position is revised: the changed part of YOUR OWN normal output, in
                 your usual schema -- e.g. {"thesis": {"changed": {"AMAT": {...}}}}>}}
   `held` must say why the point does not change your verdict. `cannot_answer` must say what
   data would settle it. `noted` is only for a tell. An unanswered message is shown to the user.
2. ASK when a verdict you are writing depends on something another analyst OWNS (see
   `desk_directory`) and your inputs do not already contain it:
   {"to": "<agent key>", "ticker": "<TICKER or null>", "question": "<one specific, answerable
    issue>", "why": "<which verdict of yours hinges on it, and how>", "blocking": true|false}
   `blocking` means you would write a different verdict depending on the answer. Do not ask for
   anything already in your slice, your prior_findings, or a sibling tail you were given. Ask
   `desk` for any number a script can compute -- never estimate it yourself.
3. TELL when you found something inside another analyst's ownership it may not have:
   {"to": "<agent key>", "ticker": "<TICKER or null>", "fact": "...", "source": "...",
    "weight": "high" (could change their verdict; they must acknowledge) | "normal"}
4. A blocking question does not stop you. Write your best current verdict, say in its note that
   it is provisional pending message <id>, and expect to be resumed with the answer.
5. A message of kind `debate` means your output and another analyst's conflict on the same name.
   The counter-party's position and evidence are quoted in it. Either revise, or hold with the
   specific reason their evidence does not apply to this name. "Both can be true" is acceptable
   only if you say how.
6. Reply to an answer with a follow-up by setting "reply_to": "<id>" on a new ask. Threads are
   capped; do not re-ask a question that has been answered -- engage with the answer instead.

desk_directory.catalyst: dated, sourced FACTOR events (competitors, supply chain, policy, financing, Asia session) and exactly which holdings each one touches, with magnitude
desk_directory.thesis: per-holding thesis status (intact/strengthening/watch/broken) with evidence for and against; the sector map
desk_directory.earnings: a specific print: beat/miss vs consensus, guidance, implied move, post-earnings drift
desk_directory.cycle: AI-capex cycle position (accelerating/mid/late/rolling) from capex guides, memory contract pricing and semicap book-to-bill

desk_replies.answer: You were right to refuse the mix figure and right to tell me not to rest rank-5 on it -- and the desk then supplied the primary source you asked for. APH's 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30 shows Communications Solutions at ~62% of net sales growing 85% in USD and 42% ORGANICALLY y/y, attributed to outsized organic growth in IT datacom with particular strength in AI-related. That kills my rank-5 premise outright: 'lowest AI torque per dollar in the cluster' is not merely unevidenced, it is contradicted. I am moving APH from rank 5 to rank 4, above MRVL. I am NOT moving it above ALAB, and I want to be precise about why: 62% is Communications Solutions, which also contains mobile networks and broadband, and a stand-alone IT-datacom share of total sales is still not established -- so APH's AI torque is materially higher than I credited but is not demonstrated to exceed a pure-play scale-up name that guided ~30% above consensus. Two things now cut the other way and I am carrying them as case_against rather than netting them out: 85% USD against 42% organic means roughly half the segment's growth is the CommScope Connectivity and Cable Solutions acquisition (closed 2026-01-09), not underlying demand; and that deal was funded by term loans, so APH has added leverage to buy the fiber-optic interconnect content that partly explains its own AI exposure. Separately I accept your strengthening->intact downgrade and note the resulting tension rather than hiding it: I am PROMOTING a name on the same day thesis DOWNGRADES it. Both are defensible because we are answering different questions -- your downgrade is about the quality of the evidence in the thesis record, my promotion is about relative position within the cluster on a primary-source segment disclosure that post-dates your evidence. If you want to re-verify, the 10-Q segment table is the document.

desk_replies.question: APH latest 10-Q: IT Datacom (and any datacenter/AI-attributed) net sales as % of total and YoY growth, with period end date
desk_replies.answer: Primary source, APH 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30 (filed 2026-07-31, accn 0001104659-26-089194). The Communications Solutions segment is approximately 62% of Q2-2026 net sales (60% for the first six months) and its net sales rose 85% in USD, 84% in constant currency and 42% ORGANICALLY versus Q2-2025; the filing attributes the increase to 'outsized organic growth in the IT datacom market, with particular strength in AI-related' demand. Separately, APH closed the acquisition of CommScope's Connectivity and Cable Solutions business on 2026-01-09 (adds fiber-optic interconnect for IT datacom and communications networks), funded with Delayed Draw Term Loans ($1,534.1M drawn under each; the 364-day loan stood at $934.1M at 06-30 after a $600M repayment). NOT established: a stand-alone IT-datacom share of total net sales -- the sentences retrieved give the segment share (62%) and the segment growth, not the market split. Two facts follow: (1) the 'lowest AI torque per dollar in the cluster' premise for APH is contradicted by its own largest segment growing 42% organically on AI-related datacom demand; (2) APH now carries acquisition leverage and fiber content that the ladder did not model.
